title: Enterprise and security risk management framework and method
status_rationale: Business plan sections 13.02 (risk management) and 18.x (risk register summary and reassessment triggers) describe intended practice in draft. No adopted method, completed assessment or risk owner was located.
target_answer: Our risk method follows ISO/IEC 27005-style assessment within an ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF 2.0 structure: assets, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact are scored on a documented scale, including fraud and AI-agent misuse scenarios. A full assessment runs at least annually and is re-run on defined triggers (new data category, new integration, new autonomous permission, material incident, new regulated customer type). Threat models produced with Tutela for each product feed the enterprise register. The managing member owns the process; an independent advisor reviews results.
current_practice: Not established; draft plan text only.
intended_practice: Adopt method and perform first assessment before first production customer.
customer_statement: A documented risk management method and first formal risk assessment are planned but not yet completed.
open_questions: Is ISO/IEC 27005 to be seeded as a source? It is not in SEED-IDS.

title: Risk register, treatment tracking and effectiveness
status_rationale: BP section 18 is a risk register summary in draft prose. No machine-readable register linked to controls or evidence exists.
target_answer: We maintain a machine-readable risk register in which each risk has an owner, inherent and residual rating, treatment decision, linked controls (ECTL-, UNB-CTRL-) and linked evidence requirements. Treatment actions have due dates; overdue actions raise an exception automatically. Effectiveness is judged from control evidence and incident data, not from completion of tasks. Risks arising from our own size and stage (key-person dependence, limited runway, customer concentration) are in the register and summarized to customers under NDA.
intended_practice: Create register as records under Praxis with validation that every high risk links to at least one control and evidence requirement.
customer_statement: A linked risk register is planned. A summary of key risks, including our own early-stage business risks, can be discussed under NDA.

title: Risk appetite, tolerance and risk acceptance authority
status_rationale: No risk appetite statement or acceptance authority exists. Unbound requirements place risk appetite for sponsor operations with the sponsor board (UNB-GOV-001), which is distinct from Echelon's own appetite.
target_answer: The managing member has approved a risk appetite statement with measurable tolerances for security, availability, data integrity and compliance. Residual risks above tolerance can be accepted only by the managing member and only with a recorded decision; any acceptance that affects a customer's data or obligations is disclosed to that customer, who can object. Because one person may both propose and accept a risk, every acceptance above a defined rating is reviewed by an independent advisor within 30 days and the review is recorded. Risks to sponsor operations remain the sponsor board's to accept (UNB-GOV-001).
intended_practice: Adopt appetite statement and acceptance workflow using Praxis decision records.
customer_statement: A risk appetite statement and risk acceptance procedure are planned but not yet adopted.

challenge.customer_intent: Risks are accepted deliberately by someone with authority, not by default or self-interest.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Risky shortcuts are accepted quietly by the person who benefits from them.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Segregation between risk proposer and approver is impossible inside a one-person company; a signature from the same person adds little.
challenge.legally_required: No; certification criteria (ISO 27001 6.1.3) require risk owners to approve treatment plans and residual risk.
challenge.contractually_required: Sometimes, via notice obligations for risks affecting the customer.
challenge.historical_convention: Risk committee approval in larger firms.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Structural controls that make certain risks unacceptable by construction (for example SEC-DB-001 denies dynamic SQL) remove whole classes from the acceptance process.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Exceptions and acceptances are data with expiry, enforced by CI (RSK-004).
challenge.continuous_evidence: Decision records with independent reviewer attestation.
challenge.stronger_alternative: External independent reviewer plus customer disclosure for customer-affecting acceptances.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, via reviewer attestations and decision record history.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Reviewer not truly independent; disclosures not made.
challenge.conventional_cost: Risk committee: not feasible at this size.
supporting_arguments: Puts a second set of eyes where segregation is otherwise impossible.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; depends on reviewer credibility.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: An advisor has no authority to block a decision.
Customers may consider customer disclosure burdensome noise.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Policy and standard exceptions with enforced expiry
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard requires exceptions to be explicit, narrowly scoped, time-limited, approved by an accountable reviewer and accompanied by compensating controls, with no silent bypasses; Unbound SOC2-033 requires recorded exceptions with expiration. Neither is implemented.
target_answer: Every exception to a mandatory rule is a record naming the rule, scope (repository, path, environment), justification, compensating controls, approver and expiry. The build and release gates read the exception records: an expired exception makes the gate fail again, and a suppression without a matching record fails the build. Mandatory checks run in CI under branch protection that neither a human nor an AI agent can bypass without leaving an audit record; any bypass raises an alert. Open exception counts and the oldest exception age are reported monthly.
intended_practice: Implement exception records and gate integration in Praxis/CI as part of Secure Construction Standard adoption.
customer_statement: Exceptions are intended to be time-limited records enforced by build gates. This mechanism is planned and not yet implemented.

challenge.customer_intent: Exceptions do not become permanent, unmanaged holes.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Temporary waivers persist for years and are forgotten.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Spreadsheet exception logs with periodic review frequently go stale.
challenge.contractually_required: Rarely, beyond general compliance with security policy.
challenge.historical_convention: Exception register reviewed quarterly by security committee.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not possible to eliminate the need for exceptions; the gate makes expiry self-enforcing.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: CI gate reads expiry and fails builds.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Gate logs and exception register snapshots per build.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Expiry enforced by machine rather than by review meeting.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by inspecting gate configuration and build logs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Gate bypass by repository administrators; exceptions renewed by rote.
challenge.alternative_risks: Release blocked by an expired exception during an incident; needs an emergency path with post-review.
supporting_arguments: Turns a procedural control into an automatic one.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Administrators of a tiny organization can still disable the gate; detection depends on audit logs the same person controls.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Echelon's own third-party and fourth-party risk management
status_rationale: Business plan 12.02 (vendor governance) and 12.03 (strategic dependencies) are drafts. Unbound requires vendor inventory and subservice monitoring (SOC2-013, SOC2-022) and a per-tenant subprocessor register (UNB-XIN-SAS-011). No inventory or assessments exist.
target_answer: We maintain an inventory of critical vendors, derived where possible from infrastructure-as-code, SBOM and billing data so it cannot silently drift, covering cloud hosting, code hosting, CI, AI model providers, email and support tooling. Each critical vendor has a criticality rating, assessment (SOC report review including complementary user entity controls we must operate, financial check, contract review), data classes received, AI training terms, incident notice terms and an exit plan. Reviews are annual and on change. Vendor incidents affecting customers are relayed within our contractual notice period.
current_practice: Not established; vendors in use are not inventoried in any record located.
intended_practice: Build inventory and assess the cloud, code hosting and AI providers first.
customer_statement: A formal inventory and assessment of our own critical vendors, including AI model providers, is planned and not yet complete.

title: Risk assessment of AI agent use, new capabilities and model provider change
status_rationale: Unbound requires design review before new data categories, external APIs or autonomous permissions (SOC2-030) and bounded agent authority (SOC2-017, CNV-AIO-001). Echelon uses AI agents for engineering, as Praxis provenance records in these repositories show, but no documented AI risk assessment was located.
target_answer: Before an AI agent receives a new tool, permission, data class or production pathway, a recorded risk assessment covers misuse, prompt injection, data leakage, unreviewed change and loss of attribution, mapped to NIST AI RMF and the OWASP agentic threat list, and names the controls (tool brokering, least privilege, human approval, provenance). Model or provider changes are treated as changes: pinned model identifiers, evaluation against regression suites before switching, and notice to customers where processing of their data changes.
current_practice: Not established. AI agents perform engineering work in Echelon repositories; risk assessment of that use is not documented.
intended_practice: Add AI-specific triggers to the risk method and a change record for model/provider changes.
provable: Praxis provenance records show agent identities on repository work, which evidences the use but not an assessment of it.
customer_statement: AI agents are used in Echelon engineering work. A documented AI-specific risk assessment and model change procedure are planned.

title: Risk reporting to customers and scenario analysis
status_rationale: Unbound requires claims to be reconciled to evidence (SOC2-020, MON-024). No customer risk reporting or scenario analysis exists.
target_answer: Customers receive a periodic risk and control status report generated from the live register and control evidence, so it cannot drift from the internal view, with each statement tagged by status (operating, designed, planned). We run and record at least annually severe-but-plausible scenarios: loss of the founder, loss or suspension of the cloud account, ransomware or credential compromise in CI, loss of a major customer, and AI agent misuse, with the resulting actions.
intended_practice: Generate customer reports from records with Folio once the register exists.
customer_statement: Periodic customer risk reporting and scenario analysis are planned.
